statement: Let ξi = (θi, ri) and ξj = (θj, rj) be conditionally independent, identically distributed planar marks given Z. Suppose their bounded-depth records obey the preceding score calculus, and their time marginals have prefix mass exponent at least d > 0 given Z, with d ≤ 1. More precisely, at every prescribed finite collection of depths, discarding a set of vanishing average probability makes the unnormalized conditional time-interval bounds hold with exponent d and arbitrarily small losses. Assume (RW). Trim at the required depths to measures µZ dominated by the conditional mark laws. Pass to a joint subsequential limit of the needed scores and of e(t) = − log1/ρ µZ(Nρt (l(ξi, ξj))), t > 0 rational. Then, almost surely, e∗ := lim inf t↓0 e(t) t ∈ {0} ∪ [d, ∞]. (rad) If, in addition, the conditional tube supremum satisfies a uniform affine-line avoidance estimate of some positive exponent in these depth units, then e∗ ≥ d almost surely.
